families.source: UKHSA final outbreak investigation report toolkit
families.topic: outbreak report structure, evidence, recommendations, confidentiality, disclosure and legal review
evidence_points: The toolkit provides a suggested structure for detailed outbreak investigation reports.
A report may be appropriate for complex incidents, enforcement, legal proceedings or significant shared learning.
Reports should describe epidemiological, microbiological, environmental and other investigation methods and results.
Control measures and their effectiveness should be documented.
Recommendations should address prevention, surveillance, investigation, control and equity.
Confidentiality, identifiability, disclosure, legal proceedings and sign-off require explicit consideration.
The page is an official GOV.UK source for outbreak report structure, evidence, recommendations, confidentiality, disclosure and legal review and was live-checked on 31 July 2026.
The source is intended to support evidence-based, proportionate action and should be used with current local and topic-specific arrangements.
A notification, case, cluster, symptom, setting issue or checklist alone does not establish that every recommendation in Toolkit 9: final outbreak investigation report applies.
Final decisions require current incident facts, responsible-authority judgement, documented risk assessment and any applicable clinical, legal or operational evidence.

evidence_points: The toolkit provides suggested auditable standards for outbreak management.
Standards cover timely recognition and initial risk assessment.
Audit measures can assess investigation, governance, communication and control activity.
Compliance data should be derived from defined operational records.
Audit findings should be considered in the outbreak report and lessons process.
Standards are intended to support quality improvement rather than replace incident judgement.

families.topic: how VCSE groups and affected settings participate in IMTs, handle information and follow actions
families.page_title: A guide to incident management teams (IMTs)
evidence_points: The guide is written for voluntary, community and social enterprise groups and affected settings.
An IMT brings organisations together to assess risk, make decisions and agree plans.
Participants may include public health, healthcare, environmental health, local authorities and community representatives.
Sensitive information should be handled under confidentiality and data-protection requirements.
Members can provide community or setting intelligence and help shape accessible messages.
Minutes record decisions and actions, and a later debrief may identify learning.
